name: Satsuma mandarins
tile_uses: The jar, the weekend braise, mornings, the drink
why_now: Satsumas are among the first California citrus of the season, and they start arriving in November — sweet, seedless, and so loose in their skins they peel in one piece. They're at their best now and through December.
how_to_choose: Heavy for their size; light ones have started to dry out
A puffy, loose peel is normal for a satsuma, not a sign of age
Bright orange, with a little green near the stem still fine
buy_this_much: A 2-lb bag, about ten. One goes into the jar and the braise; the rest get eaten out of hand.
price_note: Usually sold in bags or by the pound; the bags are cheaper and just as good.

flavor_paths.name: Peeled
flavor_paths.description: Out of hand. The reason to buy a bag.

flavor_paths.name: Zested
flavor_paths.description: Over a braise or yogurt, right at the end.

flavor_paths.name: Peel in a jar
flavor_paths.description: Strips in the pickled fennel; the oil in the peel perfumes the brine.

weekday_uses: Segments over the roast chicken and cauliflower
weekend_use: Juice and zest into the weekend braise, where they keep a rich pot bright.
storage: In the fridge, loose, for up to two weeks. On the counter they're fine for a few days.
one_thing_to_learn: A satsuma's loose peel is the variety, not age. Judge them by weight instead: a heavy one is full of juice.
